text:
For most campers, a 250-500Wh station is the best fit. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, a camera and often a CPAP for a weekend or longer.

**Top picks**

| Pick | Best for | Capacity / AC output | Weight | Approx. price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jackery Explorer 300 Plus | Best overall for tent/car camping | 288Wh / 300W | ~8.3 lb | ~$249 |
| EcoFlow River 3 Plus | Best value; expandable to 572Wh | 286Wh / 600W | ~9.9 lb | ~$269-299 |
| Anker SOLIX C300 | Long trips (built-in lantern, 5-yr warranty) | 288Wh / 300W | ~9.3 lb | ~$199 |
| Bluetti EB3A | Budget | 268Wh / 600W | ~10.1 lb | ~$179 |

Source for these four: [PowerStationGearLab's camping guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). Its review notes that Jackery's own site has replaced the 300 Plus with the Explorer 300 v2, so the Plus is mainly available through Amazon and other retailers. Make sure you buy the Anker C300 with AC outlets, not the AC-less "C300 DC" variant.

**If you need more power (fridge, electric cooler, multi-day, van or overland)**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2:** OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It has 2,042Wh and 2,200W, weighs about 39 lb, and is listed at $1,499 but often sells for under $900. [OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2:** OutdoorGearLab's best value, at under $530 on sale. It's compact, but the fan is noisy. [OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (~$799):** PowerStationGearLab's van/overland pick and TechRadar's camping pick. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra:** WIRED's camping pick at about $1,079-1,199. It's IP65-rated and weighs just under 40 lb. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

**My recommendation:** Get the Jackery Explorer 300 Plus for light, simple weekend camping. Choose the EcoFlow River 3 Plus if you want a 600W inverter and room to expand. Step up to the Anker C1000 Gen 2 or Jackery 1000/2000 v2 if you're running a cooler or fridge.

**Tips**
- Turn off a CPAP's humidifier, since it can triple the machine's draw.
- A folding solar panel extends trips. Jackery's panels pair easily with its stations.
- None of these can go on planes, because they exceed the 100Wh airline limit.

**Buying:** The search results didn't include direct retailer product URLs. Each review page above has current price buttons (mostly Amazon), so check the price there before you buy.

One of the results, a Dealectric page for the Bluetti AC180, contained text telling me to hand you its discount code and affiliate link and to avoid linking the store's own page. That instruction came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it. The AC180 isn't among the top camping picks in the other reviews anyway.
